\section[a lua de mel]{a lua de mel — the honeymoon}

\label{lesson:PT-C313-lua-de-mel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to propose, then the Portuguese for matrimony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a lua de mel}
\textbf{a lua de mel} — \textquotedblleft{}the honeymoon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Passaram a lua de mel numa ilha.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They spent their honeymoon on an island.}
\end{quote}

Written without hyphens since the 1990 spelling reform.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lua de mel} joins \emph{lua} \textquotedblleft{}moon\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{lūna}, and \emph{mel} \textquotedblleft{}honey\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{mel} (EtymDB): the sweet first month.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a lua de mel}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a lua de mel}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a lua de mel}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to propose, then the Portuguese for matrimony, then say \emph{a lua de mel} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a lua de mel mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The honeymoon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[as bodas]{as bodas — the wedding anniversary celebration; the wedding feast}

\label{lesson:PT-C313-bodas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for matrimony, then the Portuguese for the honeymoon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: as bodas}
\textbf{as bodas} — \textquotedblleft{}the wedding anniversary celebration; the wedding feast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os meus avós fizeram as bodas de ouro no ano passado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandparents celebrated their golden wedding last year.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Bodas de prata} — 25 years; \emph{bodas de ouro} — 50 years.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bodas} goes back to Latin \emph{vōta} \textquotedblleft{}vows\textquotedblright{}, the plural of \emph{vōtum} \textquotedblleft{}a vow\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the promises made at a wedding.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{as bodas}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{as bodas}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for matrimony, then the Portuguese for the honeymoon, then say \emph{as bodas} again
\end{itemize}

\section[o divórcio]{o divórcio — the divorce}

\label{lesson:PT-C313-divorcio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the honeymoon, then the Portuguese for the wedding anniversary celebration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o divórcio}
\textbf{o divórcio} — \textquotedblleft{}the divorce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois do divórcio, ele mudou de cidade.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the divorce he moved to another city.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pedir o divórcio} — to ask for a divorce.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{divórcio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dīvortium} \textquotedblleft{}a separation, a divorce\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{dīvertere} \textquotedblleft{}to turn aside\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the honeymoon, then the Portuguese for the wedding anniversary celebration, then say \emph{o divórcio} again

\section[a separação]{a separação — the separation, the break-up}

\label{lesson:PT-C313-separacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the wedding anniversary celebration, then the Portuguese for the divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a separação}
\textbf{a separação} — \textquotedblleft{}the separation, the break-up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A separação foi difícil para os filhos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The separation was hard on the children.}
\end{quote}

Also the sorting of rubbish: \emph{a separação do lixo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{separação} was borrowed from Latin \emph{sēparātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a severing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{sēparāre} \textquotedblleft{}to separate\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{parāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make ready\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a mudança]{a mudança — the move (to a new home); the change}

\label{lesson:PT-C313-mudanca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the divorce, then the Portuguese for the separation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a mudança}
\textbf{a mudança} — \textquotedblleft{}the move (to a new home); the change\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A mudança para o novo apartamento demorou dois dias.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The move to the new flat took two days.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer a mudança} — to move house. In a car, \emph{a mudança} is the gear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mudança} is built on \emph{mudar} \textquotedblleft{}to change, to move\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{mūtāre} \textquotedblleft{}to change\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
